items: Attach an explicit redistribution and derivative-use license to the exact code and data release.
Provide checksum-pinned copies of eez_delta_k_df.rds and global_cc_1nation_manuscript_2019Feb12.rds, plus the realistic-adaptation raw counterpart used to build the published outputs.
Provide the executable model code and dependency lock that derive stock-year biomass, harvest, price, cost, effort, and profit from inputs, rather than only downstream formatting scripts.

Provide stock/species, EEZ/territory/sovereign, producer/fleet, landing, trade, and consumer-market keys; declare high-seas, joint/disputed, missing, zero, and out-of-scope records without imputation or renormalization.

Provide the demand system, baseline quantities/prices, elasticities or parameters, and direct consumer-surplus outputs; separately identify whether modeled profit is intended and validated as producer surplus/resource rent.

Provide same-model, same-realization annual baseline and one-ton-CO2-pulse paths (or inputs sufficient for authorized reruns) with identical geographic/stock/market masks; RCP or management contrasts are not substitutes.

Document the accounting boundary for aquaculture, terrestrial-food substitution, nutrition/mortality, coral services, and indirect/induced output so direct market surplus can be screened for GIVE additivity.

screened_candidates.geographic_coverage: 156 coastal sovereign countries, 779 single-species stocks, and 58.2% of reported 2012 global catch; released CSVs also contain ABNJ, Antarctica, and joint-area labels. Broad but explicitly incomplete.
screened_candidates.license_access: Paper is CC BY; repository is public but has no root LICENSE/COPYING file at the pinned commit, and the two raw inputs named by Step1 are absent. Derived country CSVs and R scripts are present.
screened_candidates.overlap_risks: Profit must not be added to output-multiplier damages; country allocation assumes biomass, catch, and profit are uniform over modeled species range; aquaculture, nutrition/mortality, terrestrial-food substitution, and trade incidence remain outside the model.
screened_candidates.pulse_compatibility: RCP pathways and management contrasts are not a same-realization baseline versus one-ton-CO2 pulse pair.
screened_candidates.response_semantics: RCP scenario projections of species distribution, carrying capacity, biomass, catch, and profit under management adaptations; not a marginal emissions pulse.
screened_candidates.title: Realistic fisheries management reforms could mitigate the impacts of climate change in most countries
screened_candidates.welfare_semantics: Profit equals revenue minus fishing cost in the paper. Neither consumer surplus nor an output explicitly identified as producer surplus appears in the released source.

screened_candidates.geographic_coverage: 16 US fisheries representing 56% of current US commercial fishing revenue; not global.
screened_candidates.license_access: Official NOAA article copy is CC BY-NC 4.0; no reusable model/data package was identified in the official record.
screened_candidates.overlap_risks: Seafood consumer surplus is conceptually direct market welfare, but coverage is US-only and producer, fleet, and trade incidence are absent.
screened_candidates.pulse_compatibility: High-versus-low climate scenarios are not a marginal emissions pulse.
screened_candidates.response_semantics: Consumer-welfare response to projected thermally available habitat/landings under high and low emissions scenarios.
screened_candidates.title: Estimating the economic impacts of climate change on 16 major US fisheries
screened_candidates.welfare_semantics: Two-stage inverse demand model reports consumer surplus only; producer surplus is not supplied.

screened_candidates.geographic_coverage: Global demand regions with substantial coral reef area; reef fisheries only, not the global capture-fisheries sector.
screened_candidates.license_access: Publisher full text is subscription-restricted and no official reusable code/data archive was identified.
screened_candidates.overlap_risks: Material ecological overlap with any separate coral-reef damage module; commercial reef-fish demand must not double count coral ecosystem-service values.
screened_candidates.pulse_compatibility: RCP scenarios are not a marginal emissions pulse.
screened_candidates.response_semantics: Consumer-surplus losses from reef-fish supply changes driven by coral cover under RCP scenarios.
screened_candidates.title: Impacts of climate change and ocean acidification on coral reef fisheries: An integrated ecological-economic model
screened_candidates.welfare_semantics: Consumer surplus only; producer surplus is not supplied.

screened_candidates.geographic_coverage: Spatially resolved global grid calibrated against Large Marine Ecosystems; aggregated size classes rather than country/commodity markets.
screened_candidates.license_access: The 1.7 GB Zenodo dataset and MATLAB analysis files are CC BY 4.0.
screened_candidates.overlap_risks: No country producer/consumer/trade incidence and no commodity demand system; using harvest or revenue as welfare would double count output rather than surplus.
screened_candidates.pulse_compatibility: Could be rerun with climate forcings in principle, but the archived package does not supply a matched baseline/pulse welfare pair.
screened_candidates.response_semantics: Biomass, harvest, effort, and grid-cell profit respond to temperature, primary production, and economic forcings; the archived calibration outputs are not a climate-damage scenario or marginal pulse pair.
screened_candidates.title: Formulation, general features and global calibration of a bioenergetically-constrained fishery model
screened_candidates.welfare_semantics: Open-access fishing effort responds to average profit. No consumer demand or consumer surplus is modeled, and profit is not released as a separate producer-surplus accounting output.

screened_candidates.geographic_coverage: 887 species, 280 EEZs and high seas, 192 fishing nations, representing about 60% of reconstructed catch; broad but incomplete.
screened_candidates.license_access: Open-access article and supplement; no official reusable model/output repository with an explicit data license was identified in this bounded screen.
screened_candidates.overlap_risks: Gross revenue cannot be added to profit or output-multiplier damages; distant-water fleet allocation is not consumer incidence.
screened_candidates.pulse_compatibility: Mid-century RCP contrasts are not a marginal emissions pulse.
screened_candidates.response_semantics: DBEM maximum catch potential under RCP2.6/RCP8.5 multiplied by ex-vessel prices to obtain maximum revenue potential.
screened_candidates.title: Projected change in global fisheries revenues under climate change
screened_candidates.welfare_semantics: Revenue/landed value, not consumer or producer surplus; the authors explicitly call for full economic analysis.
